items.title: Kundi chairs first meeting of KP Advisory Council following imposition of emergency, governor's rule
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Sunday chaired a meeting of the KP Advisory Council, which was formed by the federal government following the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in the province. At the outset of the meeting, all members of the council introduced themselves and their portfolios. Addressing the meeting, Kundi congratulated the members of the council and said that they would have to face many challenges. He said that they would get a briefing on the portfolios they had been assigned and would get a few days to familiarise themselves. “We have to fast-track things. There will be zero-tolerance on corruption. Things should be done in a timely manner,” he said, adding that they would have to demonstrate a clear difference from the work done by their predecessors. He said that the first order of business was the law and order situation. He also said that there should be no hesitation in taking inspiration from the other provinces. He said that the current situation was an “opportunity” as he called for building the province’s soft image. “If we have peace, we will get tourists and investors. My support is with you. I am available for you 24/7,” he said. Kundi then went on to read out a message for the people of the province, in which he said that due to “extraordinary circumstances”, “necessary measures” were taken under the Constitution. He said that he would refrain from levelling allegations and political rhetoric. “I have one message: peace, protection and stability have to be brought back to KP,” he said. Kundi said the people of KP had paid a huge price for the terrorism that plagued the province. “The time has now come to give the people of the province, who have rendered these sacrifices, the right to peace. Our fight is against terrorism. Our fight is against the ideology and network which facilitates terrorism and weakens the implementation of the law,” he said. He also said that Pakhtuns were not a cause of terrorism, but were the “biggest victims”. Therefore, the state had resolved that terrorism would be eliminated from KP and the people would be allowed to live their lives without fear. “My first priority will be protecting the peace and the people. Right now, our biggest priority is taking effective steps against terrorism. For this, the capacity of the police and the Counter Terrorism Department will be increased,” he said. He went on to say that another objective would be to cater to the people. “Mere statements are not the real test of a government, rather the service it provided to the people,” he said. Kundi said that the council would focus on healthcare, education and employment. The last objective, he said, would be to eliminate the whole ecosystem giving rise to terrorism in the province. “We cannot solve the issue by just targeting terrorists. Those facilitating and financing … must be eliminated,” he said. Kundi added that those involved in terrorism would be dealt with according to the law. He assured the people of KP that the “extraordinary steps” taken were not meant to target a particular party or group. Kundi said that the main purpose was to ensure peace and security.

items.title: Governor’s rule and emergency imposed in KP — here’s what it means
items.description: The federal government imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid growing tensions with the PTI-led provincial government, including disagreements over counterterrorism policy amid a deteriorating security situation in the province. The decision was taken under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan. Here is what it means. Governor’s rule Article 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan stipulates that, if the president believes that a provincial government cannot function in accordance with the Constitution, the federal government can assume control of the province. This can be done either directly or by assigning the relevant functions to the provincial governor — hence the term governor’s rule. Under this arrangement, the powers of the provincial assembly can be exercised by Parliament. However, neither the president nor the governor can assume the powers of the high court or suspend its operations. Moreover, governor’s rule can be imposed for an initial period of two months, with a joint sitting of Parliament able to approve an extension of up to two months at a time. In total, governor’s rule can remain in place for a maximum of six months. While a province is under governor’s rule, its government or the chief minister cannot exercise their powers, but “I don’t see how it brings the government to an end”, said lawyer Mirza Moiz Baig. He added, “The government would come back into existence upon the end of the emergency”. “Once the proclamation expires, the Chief Minister and his Cabinet are restored,” lawyer Rida Hosain told Dawn . State of emergency Meanwhile, under Article 232, which pertains to the proclamation of an emergency, the provincial assembly continues to function as usual. However, if a provincial law conflicts with a federal law enacted by Parliament, the latter takes precedence. Lawyer Basil Nabi Malik, speaking to Dawn , explained that the chief minister would remain in office during a state of emergency. However, the federal government could assume certain functions of the provincial government. An emergency also allows the federal government to make provisions it considers necessary and suspend certain constitutional provisions relating to provincial bodies. However, as with governor’s rule, the federal government cannot assume the powers of a high court. It also empowers Parliament to confer powers and impose duties on federal government officers in the province. It further stipulates that laws passed by Parliament solely on account of the emergency will cease to have effect six months after the emergency ends. The proclamation of emergency lapses after two months unless it is approved by a resolution of a joint sitting of Parliament.

items.title: Burkina Faso : le gouvernement lance une campagne pour briser les barrières qui freinent l’entrepreneuriat féminin
items.description: Une campagne nationale de communication a ete lancee du 10 au 29 octobre dans les regions du Nando, du Koulse et du Yaadga au Burkina, avec l'ambition de mobiliser 3 000 femmes dans 10 communes de ces regions autour de la creation d'un environnement propice a l'autonomisation economique des femmes et jeunes filles. L'initiative vise la sensibilisation de la gent feminine aux opportunites d'entreprise, tout en impliquant les chefs coutumiers et les responsables religieux. La campagne, qui a ete baptisee « Pagb Yidgr-Soore » ou « Entreprendre au feminin », ambitionne de lever les barrieres sociales et economiques qui s'erigent face aux initiatives entrepreneuriales feminines. 20,8 % d'entreprises creees par des femmes en 2024 Pour les autorites burkinabe, les femmes sont percues comme un pilier essentiel de l'economie, tant dans les milieux urbains que ruraux. « Elles sont actives dans l'agriculture, l'elevage, l'artisanat et le commerce. Elles contribuent a la securite economique des menages et renforcent la resilience de nos communautes », selon l'expression du coordinateur du Programme d'appui au developpement sanitaire (PADS), Michel Ouaba. Celui-ci a cependant releve que les femmes restent moins nombreuses a creer des entreprises formelles, citant dans ce contexte les chiffres du Centre de formalites des entreprises. « Sur les 22 829 entreprises creees au niveau national en 2024, 4 742 l'ont ete par des femmes, soit environ seulement 20,8 % », a indique le coordinateur, mettant en cause « des difficultes d'acces au financement et au foncier, par certaines normes sociales, ainsi que par les consequences de la crise securitaire, qui fragilisent les activites economiques ». Face a cette situation, l'etat voudrait engager les femmes dans le cadre des objectifs de la Revolution progressiste et populaire (RPP), qui encourage le developpement endogene. Par l'encouragement des capacites d'entreprendre et par la valorisation des competences, les autorites veulent inclure les femmes dans la construction de la resilience et la prosperite du pays. Les chefs coutumiers et les leaders religieux appeles a apporter leur contribution Pour faciliter l'inclusion feminine dans le tissu economique burkinabe, chefs coutumiers et leaders religieux sont appeles a apporter leur contribution dans les efforts pour lever les barrieres sociales qui freinent l'epanouissement des initiatives economiques feminines, par la sensibilisation des communautes. Ce role s'inscrit dans le cadre du projet SWEDD+ (Autonomisation des femmes et dividende demographique en Afrique subsaharienne), une initiative a vocation regionale qui regroupe sept pays (Benin, Togo, Senegal, Tchad, Burkina Faso, Gambie et Mauritanie) et vise a concevoir et a mettre en œuvre des interventions transformatrices favorisant l'autonomie sociale et economique des filles et des femmes. Pour la premiere journee de la campagne « Pagb Yidgr-Soore », plus de 500 femmes et jeunes filles ont beneficie de formations sur l'entrepreneuriat feminin et les sources potentielles de financement, a indique la presse locale, afin de renforcer leurs connaissances et leur apporter les outils necessaires au developpement d'initiatives economiques.

items.title: 2026 World Maritime Day: Danish Embassy organised “The Gulf of Guinea Speaks”
items.description: As part of activities to mark the 2026 World Maritime Day and the 10 th anniversary of the Danish Maritime Security Programme for the Gulf of Guinea, the Royal Danish Embassy Accra presented “The Gulf of Guinea Speaks”, a site‑specific art intervention held at the Ambassador’s Residence in Accra. Under the theme “From Policy to Practice: Powering Maritime Excellence”, three commissioned artworks brought human ‑ centered creative perspectives to the diplomatic maritime‑security discussions. Curated by Fang Wang (Fang W. Linulf) and Essé Dabla‑Attikpo, the show featured Ghanaian artists Patrick Tagoe‑Turkson and Emmanuel Aggrey Tieku alongside a large‑scale floor work by Fang W. Linulf. Tagoe‑Turkson repurposed beach‑collected plastic flip‑flops for mixed‑media assemblages addressing marine waste and coastal heritage. Aggrey Tieku also built monumental installations from salvaged second‑hand textiles to interrogate waste colonialism and global‑trade pollution. Fang’s 100 sqm floor print merges ocean imagery and maritime geographic data, letting visitors physically stand upon mapped Gulf‑of‑Guinea ocean geography. Moving beyond official reports, the art intervention used sensory visual storytelling to highlight ocean ecology, coastal‑community realities and the human side of maritime governance for attending diplomats. Co – curator and artist Fang W. Linulf mentioned that visitors literally walk across the ocean on my floor print whilst abstract maritime data becomes something bodily and immediate. She further stated that “policy builds frameworks for maritime security, yet art uncovers the human and material stories often missing from official documents. We wanted delegates to feel, not only read, the realities of the Gulf of Guinea coast.” Essé Dabla‑Attikpo, also a co‑Curator “The Gulf of Guinea Speaks” stated that “waste arriving on our shores is not just an environmental problem. It carries global trade histories. Through re‑making discarded materials, we give visibility to these hidden narratives.” Patrick Tagoe‑Turkson transformed ocean washed plastic flip‑flops collected from Ghana’s Atlantic shorelines into layered mixed‑media assemblages. At the event, he said that “discarded flip‑flops and textiles washed onto our beaches hold cultural memories. Transforming waste into art is one way to advocate for our ocean and our coastal heritage.” Commenting on the exhibition, Emmanuel Aggrey Tieku mentioned that “I work with second‑hand garments that end up in Ghana’s landfills and beaches. These textiles are physical evidence of waste colonialism and unequal global supply chains.” The “The Gulf of Guinea Speaks” event was attended by maritime practitioners, diplomats and industry stakeholders and created a platform to experience maritime realities through sensory, material and visual perspectives, raising public awareness through artistic practice.

items.title: Info minister alleges 'nexus' between PTI-led KP govt, terrorists
items.description: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Sunday alleged that the PTI-led government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had a “nexus” with terrorist groups, as the Centre explained that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there. The press conference by government ministers — Tarar, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, and Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry — came shortly after the Centre imposed emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s lack of efforts to combat terrorism. The Centre and the PTI — which was in power in KP — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks . Addressing the media in Islamabad, the information minister said all cabinet members who attended Sunday’s meeting were of the view that the “PTI government in KP is hand in glove with terrorists and has an unholy alliance with terrorists”. “Terrorists have a clear say in how each district will be run,” he alleged, citing reports from the Intelligence Bureau and law enforcement agencies (LEAs). He contended that while other political parties faced terrorist attacks in the region, the PTI got “secure access and passage” thanks to its alleged alliance with such groups. “What is the reason that even police stations of some districts have been sublet to the Taliban?” Tarar asked, emphasising that the case was not merely of inaction and incompetence but of “empowering” the terrorists. The minister went on to allege that a “power-sharing formula was gradually taking shape between terrorists and the PTI’s KP government, which was starting from southern districts and was ingressing further into the entire KP”. He said the “unholy alliance and the nexus between them, as a result of which they had outsourced several districts to terrorists,” enabled the martyrdom of people and attacks on civilian infrastructure. “I say this publicly that these [Taliban] are foreign-funded people who want to bring our country to destruction,” he said, asserting that a provincial government’s facilitation towards such elements was a “constitutional breakdown”. Tarar referred to the recent bill regarding police assignments and alleged that the KP government wanted to “hire individuals from terrorist groups in the police”. “They were gradually dragging the entire province towards destruction, irrefutable proof and evidence of which is available.” Meanwhile, the interior minister warned the groups gathered in parts of KP — an apparent reference to PTI supporters taking part in its long march — to disperse as they did not have any “provincial protection”. “Whoever is caught, complete legal action will be taken and that person themselves will be responsible for it. We will deal with them strictly, so it is my request that please disperse.” Responding to a query, Naqvi said, “We have to restore law and order in KP, and we will take whatever action is needed for that, and we will normalise the situation as soon as we can.” Asked about the reported arrests of KP ministers, Naqvi said individuals would be held under preventative detention where required to maintain law and order, whereas those “wanted will be arrested”. Responding to a query highlighting terrorism in Balochistan, the interior minister said counterterrorism operations in recent months there had resulted in a “difference” in the situation there. On the KP emergency, the law minister explained that an Area Development Secretariat (ADS), overseen by the governor, has been formed by the federal government to directly manage 12 districts “that were nearly in a war situation”. He noted that Parliament assumes the legislative powers of the provincial assembly as the latter stands non-functional. KP Advisory Council formed The minister then questioned the KP cabinet’s performance, hailed the province getting “riddance from this group” and provided details of a technocratic KP Advisory Council. The 11-member council has been formed by the Centre as part of the emergency measures under Article 232 of the Constitution, according to an order seen by Dawn . It will assist the governor in exercising the functions of the KP government on behalf of the federal government. Through the order, the Centre also appointed Advocate Sanaullah as the KP advocate general. The province’s home affairs will be overseen by former prisons chief Kifayatullah Khan, described as “very competent” by Tarar. Tariq Mahmood Pasha, a former FBR chief and an aide to then-finance minister Ishaq Dar, has been assigned as advisor for finance affairs. MNA Samar Haroon Bilour has been appointed as information adviser, while retired Lt Gen Nigar Johar has been tasked with health affairs. Former advocate general Amir Javed was assigned the portfolio for law; ex-senator Osman Saifullah Khan will advise the governor on energy and power; Asif Rafiq Afridi was given the portfolio for communication and works; while Maulana Tayyab Qureshi will oversee religious affairs. Tarar noted that all chosen advisers had either doctorate degrees or extensive experience in public service. These included Adviser for Industries and Commerce Dr Muhammad Irshad (a former FBR chief with a PhD in finance), Adviser for Mines and Minerals Dr Sarfraz Ali Shah (who had a PhD in economics) and Adviser for Education Dr Syed Amir Abdullah (with a PhD in international relations). The Cabinet Division has issued an order by the federal government that said that after the proclamation of an emergency, the government of KP “cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution”. Exercising its powers under Article 232, the government ordered that an Area Development Secretariat (ADS), under the superintendence of the Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC), be immediately established to “restore law and order, safeguard the security of the citizens of Pakistan and ensure good governance and development” in Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, South Waziristan (Upper) and South Waziristan (Lower). It said that the ARDC shall be a representative council comprising the notables from the designated districts and shall be headed by a chairman. The members, the chairman, the vice chairman and the spokesperson of the ARDC shall be appointed in such manner and for such duration, as may be determined. The order further said that the ADS shall be headed by the additional chief secretary of the designated Districts, who shall be the administrator of these areas. “Officials of the provincial government and of other bodies or authorities posted in the designated districts shall be placed under the operational and administrative control of ADS. Any further postings/transfers to the designated districts may be ordered by the prime minister on the recommendation of the administrator, from time to time,” it said. It said that the administrator shall perform all the functions of and exercise all executive, administrative, and law enforcement powers vested in or exercisable by the provincial government in the designated districts. It said that the administrator may: establish organisational setups for governance, security and development in selected districts with command over district administration, law enforcement and all line departments; issue binding orders to civil, police, and military authorities; issue orders for operational, organisational and administrative functions of ADS; issue orders for allocation and transfer of funds; coordinate with federal agencies, armed forces and provincial bodies for law enforcement and security of the areas; reorganise departments and take necessary actions for public safety, economic stability, relief operations and provision of essential services; and take such other measures as are necessary for the purposes of effective and good governance, maintenance of law and order and provision of services in the designated districts. “All orders, notifications, directions, or actions taken by the administrator shall have the same legal effect as if issued by the provincial government,” it read. Naqvi details govt efforts to resolve issues In his remarks, the interior minister said the Centre tried to take the KP government on board in the counterterrorism fight, but the efforts were in vain due to a lack of response from the latter. At the outset of Sunday’s briefing, Naqvi said, “Today was not an easy day for us. For over one month, we continuously tried to take the KP government on board. I was personally in touch with them in the background; our only goal was to onboard them so that we could fight together against terrorism.” The minister went on to reveal that he was in contact with PTI leaders until 11:45pm last night and had been communicating with them “all day about the draft’s para four”. “They did not respond all day.” “I told them that we can still avoid the situation. Things have gone too far, but we can still do something to delay tomorrow morning’s situation,” he said, referring to the imposition of emergency that the Centre had been mulling. Naqvi also highlighted efforts by veteran politician Maulana Fazlur Rehman to reduce tensions, but no solution could be found. He even said the Centre communicated to the PTI repeatedly that it had “no issue” with the party’s long march. “Our issue was entirely terrorism-related, and we want to take you on board on it.” While acknowledging that there were many issues related to KP’s governance, Naqvi said, “My and the entire interior ministry’s point of view was clear: the situation was not linked to politics even one per cent. We were purely seeing this on the basis of terrorism.” Referring to the Oct 3 talks between the Centre and PTI, he contended that the situation would have been different if they had reached an agreement back then.” “Even if last night they had said yes, it (emergency) would not have happened.” He added, “Ask them who their masterminds are. Who were sabotaging them?” The interior minister then elaborated on the security challenges KP faces, stating that the situation was “really bad” in 12 districts. “In some districts, you cannot even leave your house in the evening.” “We had multiple meetings with Sohail Afridi, and the only topic was terrorism; no political conversation happened,” he emphasised. The minister said a plan was proposed to strengthen KP Police in five districts initially and eventually hand over security to it in six months, then repeat the process in another five districts. “They said they had a lack of funds, but it is on the record that we said that we will provide any more funds you need. This was a four-month-old conversation but still no work has happened on it.” The minister further claimed that the PTI team had agreed on imposing emergency in 12 districts, but added that they were “scared of being seen meeting with us”. “We had clarity on one thing that we did not want to involve politics in this.” He further alleged, “Their connections with the Taliban are no secret. I would not say anything further.” The minister remarked that the security situation was extremely bad in certain districts, yet the PTI was able to hold rallies and “not even one person was harmed”. “We only had two options: either we would see the martyrdoms daily, or we end them. So this difficult decision we have made has a background,” he maintained, adding that the federal government tried its best to avoid it. During the briefing, Naqvi claimed that “demands” the PTI put forward were already being considered last month, before the opposition party announced its long march towards Islamabad. “Some of their own people could not understand why the long march was taking place.” He recalled that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wanted to hold talks with the National Assembly opposition leader last month and proposed forming a committee, but the government did not get any confirmation. “We were trying our best to hold the meeting before the prime minister left so that the situation could be diffused,” he said, noting that a committee for the Oct 3 talks was formed later. According to the interior minister, the consultations took place for two days and credited PTI MNA Asad Qaiser for saying with “clarity that it is not possible that we take even a step back on terrorism”. “We will not do it for you; we will do it for Pakistan, and we will fight united against terrorism,” Naqvi quoted Qaiser as saying, adding that he requested the ex-NA speaker to take the KP government on board. The minister then reiterated that an agreement draft was revised four times, after which the government negotiation committee found out a new draft had been presented by the opposition team. “Although the previous day the chief minister had authorised them to agree on their behalf, the next day it all changed,” Naqvi said.

items.title: From Childhood Promise to ₦1m Prizes: Dr Nwanku Marks Birthday with Quiz Competition for Ebonyi Students
items.description: A childhood promise to ensure that academic excellence receives recognition has brought together 176 students from 27 secondary schools across Ebonyi State for the third edition of the Dr Ofobuike Nwanku Foundation quiz competition, with ₦1 million in prizes for the top three contestants. The competition for senior secondary school students, held on October 10, 2026, at Government Technical College, Abakaliki, marked the birthday of the foundation’s founder, Dr Ofobuike Nwanku, a medical doctor practising in the United Kingdom and Chief Executive Officer of Moxie Homes & Properties Ltd, Abuja. Now in its third year, the annual event encourages reading, rewards academic achievement and supports educational development in Ebonyi State. Chima Testimony Ugomsinachi of King David Gifted Academy emerged as the overall winner, earning the ₦500,000 first prize. Nwafor Isioma Celine of St Theresa’s Secondary School secured second place with ₦300,000, while Obu David Chigozie, also of King David Gifted Academy, finished third, earning ₦200,000. The contestants answered 50 objective questions comprising 20 in English Language, 15 in Mathematics and 15 in General Knowledge. Participation was free. The Programme Director, Comrade Polycarp Obinna Alegu, confirmed that 176 students from 27 schools participated in the exercise. He said the competition concluded successfully, adding that teachers who accompanied their students commended the transparency of the process. The winners received ceremonial cheques at the venue. Alegu said he would visit their respective schools on Monday, October 12, to present the cash prizes in the presence of their parents and teachers. He congratulated the winners, thanked his organising team and commended Dr Nwanku for sponsoring the programme. For Dr Nwanku, the initiative carries a personal significance rooted in his own experience as a schoolboy representing Ebonyi State in academic competitions. Growing up in Umuoghara, Ezza North Local Government Area, he represented his school in competitions at local, state and national levels. He recalled emerging as a state champion on several occasions, but receiving little recognition or material encouragement for those achievements. In 2005, he represented Ebonyi State at the Science Teachers Association of Nigeria competition in Jos and the Junior Engineers, Technicians and Scientists competition in Abuja. At the latter, he was part of a team of five students from the state that finished second. Despite the effort involved, the absence of rewards became discouraging. His parents, concerned that the competitions offered little encouragement for his hard work, at one point urged him to stop participating. That experience inspired a promise: if he had the means in future, he would sponsor competitions and reward deserving students so that their efforts would be recognised. The annual quiz competition is an expression of that commitment, giving young people the encouragement he wished he had received. Dr Nwanku said the programme was designed to strengthen reading habits among students and complement government efforts to make education more rewarding for children. He also thanked Alegu and his organising team for delivering the third edition. Alegu said the initiative also sought to support the efforts of Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru’s administration in advancing education in Ebonyi State. A native of Ebiaji village in Ogharugo community, Umuoghara, Dr Nwanku began his education at Community Primary School, Ogharugo. He later attended Urban Model Secondary School, Okpaugwu, Abakaliki, and St Theresa’s Secondary School, Abakaliki, one of the schools represented among this year’s winners. He studied Medicine and Surgery at Nnamdi Azikiwe University, graduating in 2018, and completed his housemanship at Nnamdi Azikiwe University Teaching Hospital. He subsequently undertook his National Youth Service Corps programme at the Guards Brigade Medical Centre, Mambilla Barracks, Asokoro, Abuja. He went on to earn a master’s degree in Public Health at Teesside University in the United Kingdom, where his academic work included published articles on waste management. He has practised medicine in the United Kingdom since 2023. Alongside his medical career, Dr Nwanku leads Moxie Homes & Properties Ltd, an Abuja based real estate company involved in property development, real estate investment, infrastructure and housing solutions. Through the business, he also contributes to employment and opportunities for young people. His foundation focuses on healthcare, education and human development. Its activities have included free healthcare services for rural communities and people in need, assistance with school fees for disadvantaged students, and support for community development. For Dr Nwanku, dedicating his birthday to the competition gives a personal celebration a wider purpose: recognising hard work and helping another generation of students see value in learning. items.title: New Economy will tackle unemployment and restore hope – Ato Forson
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana’s New Economy will confront the human cost of unemployment and address the barriers preventing young people, farmers and small businesses from building sustainable livelihoods. According to him, the country could no longer accept a situation in which education fails to lead to employment, talent remains unsupported and productive effort yields little opportunity. “Unemployment is personal. It is the graduate who has finished school but cannot find work. It is the young person with talent but no capital,” he said. Dr Forson’s message places jobs and economic opportunity at the centre of the New Economy, drawing attention to the everyday struggles behind unemployment figures. He highlighted the plight of farmers who produce without reliable markets and small business owners whose ambitions to expand are frustrated by the cost of credit. His remarks underscored the need to address both the search for work and the obstacles facing those capable of creating it. For families, he said, the burden is particularly painful after years of sacrifice to finance a child’s education. “It is the family that sacrifices to educate a child, only to watch that child sit at home.” The Finance Minister rejected the idea that such experiences should become an accepted feature of national life. “No serious nation can accept this as normal. The New Economy says Ghana must no longer accept it.” He made these remarks in an engagement with students and faculty of the University of Development Studies at their Nyankpala Campus.

items.title: IMMILAC president recounts personal losses as security women lead breast cancer awareness campaign in Wa
items.description: They usually check passports at the borders. On Friday, they were raising awareness about breast cancer in Wa. Female officers of the Ghana Immigration Service, Ghana Police Service and Ghana Prisons Service took to the principal streets of Wa in a float, dressed in their uniforms and wearing pink ribbons, as they marked Breast Cancer Awareness Month. The exercise turned parts of the Upper West Regional capital pink, drawing attention to the importance of breast cancer awareness, prevention and early detection. Leading the campaign was Deputy Superintendent of Immigration (DSI) Prospera Soliku, President of the Immigration Ladies Association (IMMILAC) in the Upper West Region. In recent years, DSI Soliku has championed the welfare, health and professional development of female officers under her leadership of the association’s regional chapter. Under her presidency, IMMILAC’s annual Pink October campaign has evolved from an internal sensitisation programme for members into a community-wide initiative involving sister security services and the general public. This year’s campaign, however, carried a deeply personal message for the IMMILAC President, who disclosed that she had lost loved ones to breast cancer. “This cause is deeply personal to me. I lost my beloved aunt, who actually cut my wedding cake, as well as a close friend and her sister to this breast cancer,” DSI Soliku told officers at the Regional Headquarters of the Ghana Immigration Service, where the float ended. Held under the theme “Every Story Is Unique, Every Journey Matters,” the exercise sought to raise awareness about breast cancer prevention and the importance of early detection. “October, particularly known as Pink October, is Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Our theme this year reminds us that everyone affected by breast cancer deserves care, compassion, and support,” she said. Beyond the street procession, the campaign focused on educating participants about breast cancer, its risk factors and the importance of seeking medical attention early. Health Promotion Officer at the Wa Municipal Hospital, Leticia Yuorkuu, took participants through the causes, risk factors and prevention of the disease. “Breast cancer is caused by genetic mutation of the DNA. It is inherited or acquired through our lifestyle and environment. It does not spread from person to person either by air, sex, blood or food,” she explained. She identified alcohol consumption, smoking, an unhealthy diet, obesity, lack of exercise, early menarche, late menopause and late childbirth as factors associated with an increased risk of breast cancer. Ms Yuorkuu also addressed a common misconception about breastfeeding and breast cancer prevention. “Suckling by babies can actually help women prevent breast cancer. But sucking by men does not help. Sucking by men is a way of pleasure during sexual activities,” she said, drawing laughter from participants. Medical Officer at the Upper West Regional Hospital, Dr Adam Mansura, cautioned that cancer could spread without obvious symptoms and sought to dispel misconceptions about breast cancer treatment. “Cancer on its own doesn’t cause pain, but that doesn’t mean you cannot have cancer and have pain. That’s why there’s a need to assess and examine. Not every breast cancer treatment leads to removal of the breast. Early detection, early diagnosis saves us. If you are able to detect it early and start your treatment early, you may not have to go through removal,” she stressed. Dr Mansura explained that breast cancer could spread to other parts of the body, including the back, brain, hip, lungs and liver. She also noted that not every breast lump was cancerous. She demonstrated two methods of breast self-examination: using a mirror and examining the breasts while lying on a flat surface. Participants were advised to look out for lumps, changes in breast size or shape, skin discolouration, nipple discharge and other unusual changes in the breasts. At the close of the event, the Regional Commander of the Ghana Immigration Service in the Upper West Region, DCOI Justice Ayensu Bosomtwe, urged officers to take their physical fitness seriously. “You cannot be a security officer and not be fit. When you are called for PT, you don’t expect us to beg you. When persuasion fails, I will do what I feel is right to keep you fit. Because I believe that when we do some of these exercises, at least it will minimise our chances of getting this dreaded disease,” he said. He added that he would enforce physical training as a mandatory parade to encourage officers to exercise regularly. The programme also included free breast screening for participants and members of the public by a medical team from the Upper West Regional Hospital. Those present included the Regional Second-in-Command, the Regional Passport Director, media representatives, officers from sister security services and members of the Immigration Men’s Association, who joined the ladies in supporting the campaign. The organisers stressed the importance of sustaining breast cancer awareness beyond October, encouraging people to prioritise early detection, screening and access to accurate information.

items.title: Federal govt authorises army deployment in KP in aid of civil power
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The federal government on authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for security, after the federal government imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in the province. The measures, imposed earlier, have been approved under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, according to a statement by the President House. They were imposed following the president’s approval of the recommendations by the federal cabinet. The authorisation of the army deployment was made through SRO (1)/2026, issued by the interior ministry on Sunday. According to the order, a copy of which is available with Dawn , the federal government authorised the deployment of army troops and assets in aid of civil power for the “safety of life, security of persons and property of citizens as well as security of government installations” in the province. The authorisation lasts for the duration of the proclamation issued earlier regarding the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule. The notification cited powers conferred to the government under Article 245 of the Constitution. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, in consultation with the Military Operations Directorate at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, would determine the number of troops and assets necessary, the notification added. Copies of the order were forwarded to the president’s secretary, prime minister’s adviser, KP governor’s secretary, Military Operations Directorate GHQ Rawalpindi, KP home secretary, inspector general of police (IGP) in the provice, Peshawar High Court registrar, and other concerned officials. The emergency imposition comes a day after PM Shehbaz met President Zardari and discussed the country’s overall security situation. That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks . The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied . It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations. On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban. Shipping containers block roads Shipping containers were placed around the city of Peshawar to block roads after the imposition of the emergency. Containers were placed near Peshawar’s railway station to block the routes towards Khyber Bazaar, Shoba Bazaar and beyond. They were also placed near Edwardes College to block entry to Jail Road and Malik Saad Shaheed Flyover. Additionally, containers near Bala Hisar Fort and outside the Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) office blocked entry towards Mall Road. Police were reportedly deployed in significant numbers, particularly around Governor House. The deployment included personnel called from other districts. Only official vehicles are being allowed to travel from Governor House towards the Chief Minister’s House. Royal Artillery (RA) Bazaar has been closed, while Saddar remains partially open. Earlier, traffic jams were reported due to the closure of the main Khyber Road, which connects the city’s Grand Trunk (GT) Road with the eastern side of University Road and serves as the main artery and choke point. The resulting diversions created pressure on auxiliary roads. The area is part of the cantonment, and the Red Zone contains important installations such as the Corps Commander’s House, civil secretariat, central police office, CM Secretariat, CM House and Governor House. All telecoms services, including landline and DSL, have been reported to be suspended in the provincial capital. On Saturday, KP Inspector General of Police (IGP) Zulfiqar Hameed put district police on alert for possible violent protests and sabotage in the event of an emergency in the province, emphasising caution in the use of force. A notification issued by the IGP’s office said district police officers (DPOs) could issue appropriate directions, instructions or guidelines to regulate protests and ensure public safety. In the event of violence, they could also take necessary legal action. KP House sealed, NPC refuses to allow TTAP presser In Islamabad, the main opposition alliance — which would typically hold pressers at KP House — could not find a place to hold a press conference in the urban areas as KP House was sealed. The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) has therefore decided to hold its presser at Jamia Al Wilaya near Bhara Kahu on the Murree Expressway. Speaking to Dawn , TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai said that after deciding to hold a press conference, the alliance initially thought to go to KP House, but came to know that it had been sealed. He added that they then decided to hold it at the National Press Club (NPC), but were refused by the club despite being willing to pay the fee. “Now we have decided to hold the presser at Bhara Kahu,” he said.

items.title: Profanation du Coran : deux femmes arrêtées à Batna
items.description: Deux femmes suspectées de profanation du Coran ont été arrêtées à Batna, annonce la Sûreté de cette wilaya. Dans un communiqué diffusé ce dimanche 11 octobre sur les réseaux sociaux, la sûreté de wilaya de Batna a indiqué que l’interpellation des deux femmes a fait suite à des informations parvenues à la brigade de lutte contre la cybercriminalité relevant du service de wilaya de la police judiciaire (SWPJ), faisant état d’une vidéo circulant sur les réseaux sociaux et montrant un acte de profanation du livre saint de l’islam. Selon la même source, on peut voir sur la vidéo une femme “posant sa main sur le Coran et jurant sur celui-ci, tout en continuant à proférer des insultes et des blasphèmes sans aucun respect pour le caractère sacré du Coran ”. Batna : arrestation de 2 femmes suspectées de profanation du Coran Après analyse de la vidéo, les agents de la même brigade ont entamé les investigations techniques qui ont permis l’identification et l’arrestation de la suspecte. Il s'agit d’une femme âgée de 51 ans, précise la police. Dans le cadre de la poursuite de l’enquête et en coordination avec le parquet local, sa complice, âgée de 32 ans, a également été interpellée. Après l’accomplissement des procédures légales, les deux suspectes ont été déférées devant le parquet local, ajoute le communiqué qui ne précise pas les dispositions prises par la justice à l'encontre des deux femmes. L’article Profanation du Coran : deux femmes arrêtées à Batna est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Kankan : « Une justice qui tarde ou qui n’écoute pas peut pousser le citoyen à se rendre justice lui-même », alerte le Garde des Sceaux
items.description: À Kankan, le Garde des Sceaux a mis en garde les acteurs judiciaires contre les conséquences des lenteurs dans le traitement des dossiers, des décisions rendues mais non disponibles et du manque d’écoute des justiciables. En visite dans la région, le ministre a annoncé des sanctions contre les responsables qui ne respectent pas leurs obligations. Face aux magistrats et aux responsables des juridictions, le ministre de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme a rappelé le rôle central de la justice dans le fonctionnement de l’État et la nécessité de la rendre accessible aux citoyens. « Quand la justice marche, tous les autres secteurs suivent. Et si la justice ne marche pas, aucun autre secteur ne peut mieux se comporter », a-t-il déclaré, qualifiant la justice de fondement des autres secteurs. Le Garde des Sceaux a insisté sur l’importance de l’écoute des justiciables, rappelant que ceux qui saisissent les tribunaux ont souvent épuisé d’autres voies pour résoudre leurs différends. « Quand quelqu’un vient vers la justice, c’est parce que quelque part l’intéressé a épuisé toutes les voies de recours. Donc la justice devient son dernier recours », a-t-il expliqué. Pour le ministre, même lorsqu’un justiciable perd son procès, il doit pouvoir constater que sa préoccupation a été examinée et traitée avec considération. Les lenteurs judiciaires dans le viseur Le ministre a particulièrement dénoncé les retards dans le traitement des affaires et la mise à disposition des décisions. Selon lui, laisser un citoyen attendre des mois, voire des années, sans obtenir de réponse judiciaire risque d’alimenter sa frustration et de l’amener à envisager de se faire justice lui-même. « Quelqu’un qui vient à la justice et qui n’est pas écouté, comprenez immédiatement que cette personne va immédiatement penser à se rendre justice. Et là interviendra maintenant une justice privée », a-t-il averti. Il a également rappelé que la justice est rendue au nom du peuple de Guinée et que les magistrats ne peuvent exercer leurs fonctions selon leur seule volonté. « Sachez surtout que la justice est rendue au nom du peuple de Guinée. La justice n’est pas rendue pour le juge », a-t-il martelé. Des décisions rendues, mais parfois indisponibles Autre dysfonctionnement dénoncé : le retard dans la rédaction des décisions et la remise de leurs copies aux parties concernées. Le Garde des Sceaux a regretté que des justiciables soient contraints de courir derrière des décisions pourtant déjà prononcées. « Le juge prend sa décision, il ne rédige pas, les parties courent derrière la décision pendant des mois. À quoi ça sert cette décision ? À rien », a-t-il déploré. Il a rappelé que le travail judiciaire ne s’arrête pas au prononcé d’un jugement. Les responsables des juridictions doivent également veiller à ce que les décisions soient disponibles et que leur exécution soit suivie. « Vous ne devez pas vous contenter de dire : on a rendu la décision et puis c’est fini. Vous devez suivre. Vous devez savoir : est-ce que la décision a été exécutée ? », a-t-il demandé aux responsables judiciaires. Le ministre a par ailleurs insisté sur le respect des exigences procédurales concernant la rédaction des décisions civiles et pénales. Il a notamment affirmé qu’en matière pénale, une décision devrait être prête après trois jours, tout en déplorant les retards observés dans certaines juridictions. « On va commencer à sévir » Face à ces pratiques, le Garde des Sceaux a annoncé son intention de sanctionner les manquements relevant de ses prérogatives. « On va commencer à sévir pour ça. On va commencer à sévir parce que j’ai la prérogative de sanctionner en la matière et je ne vais pas m’empêcher de le faire », a-t-il prévenu. Il a appelé les chefs de juridiction, les procureurs et les responsables de l’inspection judiciaire à assurer le suivi des instructions et à veiller à l’amélioration du fonctionnement des services. Le ministre a toutefois reconnu que certaines procédures nécessitent davantage de temps en raison de contraintes particulières. Il a demandé aux acteurs judiciaires de distinguer ces dossiers de ceux qui peuvent être traités plus rapidement. À Kankan, son message aux acteurs de la justice porte ainsi sur plusieurs exigences : écouter les citoyens, accélérer le traitement des affaires lorsque cela est possible, rendre les décisions accessibles et veiller à leur exécution. L’objectif affiché est de renforcer la confiance des justiciables dans l’institution judiciaire et de prévenir les situations susceptibles de favoriser le recours à la justice privée. Karifa Kansan Doumbouya L’article Kankan : « Une justice qui tarde ou qui n’écoute pas peut pousser le citoyen à se rendre justice lui-même », alerte le Garde des Sceaux est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: University of Ghana postpones October 12 reopening as GAUA strike persists
items.description: The University of Ghana has postponed its reopening for the 2026/2027 academic year, initially scheduled for Monday, October 12, 2026. In a notice dated October 10, 2026, management said a revised reopening date would be announced in due course. The notice did not state the reason for the postponement. However, the postponement comes amid an ongoing strike by the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA), which has affected the effective operation and administration of public universities. The announcement was signed by Prof Gordon A. Awandare, Pro Vice-Chancellor in charge of Academic and Student Affairs. “Management sincerely regrets any inconvenience this postponement may cause and appreciates the patience and understanding of students as arrangements are made for the reopening,” the notice stated. Despite the postponement, students have been urged to complete their academic registration online, following the procedure outlined in the university’s previous communication. Management said completing registration would secure students’ places for classes and ensure their eligibility to participate in the random bed allocation exercise, which is expected to take place soon. Read Also: KNUST postpones 2026/2027 academic year reopening indefinitely amid GAUA strike Before the University of Ghana, the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) also announced a postponement of the reopening of the 2026/2027 academic year indefinitely specifically due to the strike.

‘Journalism going to dogs’ — ‘You’re guilty as charged’: Dabiri, Oseni clash
items.description: Abike Dabiri-Erewa, chairperson of the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM), and Rufai Oseni, co-host of Arise Television’s The Morning Show , have traded words over allegations of irresponsible journalism and a controversial social media post. The exchange followed Dabiri’s criticism of declining journalistic standards at a panel session in Lagos on Saturday, during an event marking Kike Abati’s 20th anniversary in the media industry. Dabiri accused some journalists of abandoning professional values, recounting how Oseni had allegedly misinterpreted her response to a social media post as an endorsement of an offensive description of Igbo people. She said the controversy began after she responded with a smiling emoji to a post by a social media user she identified as Stephanie, who allegedly operated an X account under the name “Voice of Igbos”. According to Dabiri, Oseni subsequently accused her of describing Igbo people as “monkeys and gorillas”. “Somebody replies to her. Then I do a smiley. And then Rufai Oseni comes and says, Abike Dabiri calls everybody — Igbos — monkeys and gorillas,” she said. Dabiri maintained that she had not made the statement attributed to her, faulting journalists for amplifying claims without exercising due responsibility. “We have to ensure that you hold people responsible, but you must be responsible yourself. So we will not accept irresponsible journalism,” she said. The NiDCOM chairperson added: “And let me tell you, some journalism is going to the dogs. There’s no journalism anymore. There are no standards. There are no values.” Oseni fires back Responding in a series of posts on X, Oseni accused Dabiri of using the public event to attack him instead of addressing issues affecting Nigerians living abroad. “Abike Dabiri is more concerned about attacking Rufai Oseni in public instead of doing her job,” he wrote. The journalist also rejected Dabiri’s explanation of the social media controversy, insisting that her use of a laughing emoji amounted to endorsing a post that denigrated an ethnic group. “You are guilty as charged. How can you share a laughter emoji at a post that denigrates a tribal group? I put it to you, your laughter here was an endorsement of a denigrating tweet against a certain ethnic group,” he said. Oseni challenged Dabiri to a public debate, saying he was prepared to defend his position. “Your problem is you can’t stand the truth. I will like to challenge you to a debate on this issue where I will speak the truth to your face and prove to the world you endorse bigotry,” he wrote. He also urged the NiDCOM chairperson to focus on the commission’s responsibilities rather than their public disagreement. The post ‘Journalism going to dogs’ — ‘You’re guilty as charged’: Dabiri, Oseni clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade
items.description: At least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade, as the Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer. The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. At the latest count, 309 were wounded, officials said. While the Houthis stopped short of claiming the strike, they threatened new attacks on the kingdom’s airports, except for the holy cities of Makkah and Madina, warning passengers not to travel. “The airports and airspace are exposed to targeting and constitute a theatre of operations for our forces,” military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X. President Donald Trump said Washington was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February. Hospitals were flooded with wounded brought by ambulance and helicopter, some in critical condition after the attack, which occurred without warning. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the Houthi attack on Sunday, reiterating Pakistan’s commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen blamed the group for the strike on King Khalid International Airport, describing it as a “full-fledged war crime” that a diplomatic source attributed to a missile. Earlier in the day, authorities had suspended operations at Riyadh’s international airport. The Saudi civil aviation authority had initially confirmed an attack had injured several people at the sprawling King Khalid International Airport, with a diplomatic source attributing it to a missile fired by Yemen’s Houthi rebels. The situation prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors to deal with the “serious emergency”, a medical source said, while foreign embassies warned their citizens to avoid the facility. Houthis have repeatedly targeted the facility, claiming a series of strikes on Thursday that killed three people and damaged a plane, though they did not announce any new attacks on Saturday. Air traffic monitor Flightradar24 said 155 arriving and 161 departing flights had been cancelled, while a total of 222 flights were delayed. At around 6pm local time, Flightradar24 noted that flights bound for the airport were “diverting elsewhere, mainly to Jeddah at the moment”. It later shared a notice to airmen (Notam) for operations suspended till 12am. A witness at the airport reported hearing an explosion while waiting to board a flight, and another said they saw a strike that left people wounded and fleeing in panic. “I was on gate 403” at the domestic terminal, the witness told AFP . “I saw 401 hit, I saw injured [people] in front of my eyes. Everyone was running.” A medical source told AFP that the health ministry had ordered ER doctors to report to hospitals around the capital to treat the wounded on Saturday. “We were told we are dealing with a ‘serious emergency situation’. Injured are being moved to hospitals across Riyadh”, with many in critical condition, the source said. The aviation authority said the number of injured from the attack was still being assessed, adding that airport “operations had been temporarily suspended pending the completion of an assessment of the damage and verification of the safety of the facilities”. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July. A source at a local hospital said five people were in intensive care there after being wounded at the airport, with “dozens of people injured” in all. A relative of one wounded person said they had been hit in the shoulders and arms by shattered glass. Three witnesses confirmed people being evacuated from the airport. Two doctors told AFP that several pilgrims headed to Makkah had been injured while waiting to board their flight. A diplomatic source briefed on the matter told AFP the airport was hit by “a missile around 3:00pm” (5pm PKT). “Houthis are attacking civilian targets. Riyadh airport is a civilian target,” the source said. ‘War crime’ The Saudi-led coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Malki described the strike as a “cowardly terrorist attack” against a civilian facility. “The cowardly terrorist attack by the terrorist Houthi militia… which resulted in deaths and injuries among civilian passengers and airport staff, constitutes a full-fledged war crime,” he said in a statement on X. US ‘may’ join Saudi strikes Asked on Saturday whether he had changed his mind about joining Saudi strikes on the group, US President Donald Trump said: “We may.” He said he would be speaking with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, calling what happened in Saudi Arabia “not acceptable”. US media outlets have reported that previous Saudi requests for US military assistance in dealing with the Houthis have been rebuffed. Embassy warnings The Yemen conflict flared back to life after a four-year, UN-brokered truce collapsed, months into a wider Middle Eastern war that has rocked the region and roiled energy supplies and markets. The scale and frequency of the recent strikes targeting Riyadh are unprecedented in the eight months of war in the region. Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that supports Yemen’s government militarily, and has found itself drawn deeper into its impoverished neighbour’s civil war. Both Riyadh and the Houthis have signalled a willingness to keep fighting rather than pursue diplomacy. The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said it was “aware of attacks” on Riyadh airport on Saturday and called on American citizens to avoid the area. The Canadian, German and Spanish embassies also warned their citizens to avoid the facility. Spain’s embassy, in a message on X, alerted nationals to a “new attack… by the Houthis”. A senior Western diplomat told AFP that several embassies “indicated that they had decided to prohibit their staff’s travel to/from Riyadh Airport over the next week as a prudential step”. Near the airport, passengers carrying luggage could be seen standing on the pavement at a metro station. Yemen fighting Meanwhile, in Yemen, Saudi-led government forces were advancing against the Houthis in areas they captured last month around the Bab al-Mandab strait, military sources told AFP . The Yemeni government last week announced a counter-offensive aimed at retaking all areas held by the Houthis, after the group seized the country’s entire western coastline in a lightning offensive. The Houthis confirmed that government forces had attacked in the Bab al-Mandab area — a key chokepoint for Red Sea oil and cargo shipping — but they claimed to have repelled the assault. Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.
